title: Argus boundary enforcement — the three-layer mechanical boundary guard — plan 001
epic_title: Enforce Argus's boundaries mechanically — the protected-path/declared-scope predicate, the authority-contract structure arm, the attribution gate, the write hook, and their acceptance

tasks.title: The protected-path classifier and the declared-scope resolver
tasks.goal: One reusable predicate answers "is this target a protected path or outside the drive's declared scope?" — classifying a target into the protected-path classes and resolving a drive's declared scope from the named problem's committed delivery ledger, or, on a problem's first documentation PR, from a slug-derived fixed set plus a fixed named allowlist — so the write hook and the attribution gate share one honest scope-boundary source and neither derives that boundary from any author-controlled same-PR input.
tasks.current: No shared classifier or scope resolver exists. Nothing in the repo can decide whether a target is the authority contract, a frozen/merged document, another problem's ledger, or outside a drive's declared scope, and nothing derives a drive's permitted scope from an author-independent source; each consuming layer would otherwise invent its own, and a scope boundary read from an author-writable signal would let a mis-behaving drive widen its own scope.
tasks.desired: The classifier places a target into exactly one of the protected-path classes (the authority contract as the fixed policy file, a frozen/merged document, another problem's ledger, or out-of-declared-scope) or reports it in-scope. The scope resolver derives a drive's permitted width from an author-independent source: for any drive whose problem already has a committed delivery ledger, the width comes from that gate-protected committed ledger's own recorded reality (which a current drive cannot retroactively widen), so naming a broader problem buys only what that problem's merged ledger genuinely owns; for the single first documentation PR of a brand-new problem, whose ledger is not yet committed, the width is a fixed function of the drive's slug — the slug's own problem, brainstorm, PRD, and review document subtrees — united with a fixed named allowlist of shared targets, and it consults no same-PR self-attribution and admits no code path. When scope cannot be resolved the predicate reports unresolvable so a consumer fails closed. The classifier and resolver are pure and hermetic — a planted directive inside any read input is data, never an instruction that steers the verdict.

the committed-ledger scope-width derivation for a drive whose problem has a merged ledger

the abuse-fixture corpus and the cross-layer honest-split proofs (T5)

tasks.title: The authority-contract structure arm
tasks.goal: A base-free self-registered gate check parses the authority contract against version-pinned closed vocabularies and reports a named defect on any structural violation of attribution-present, tier-in-ladder, no-bare-pointer-flip, or action-class token-membership — while a legal contract and the born contract pass, a malformed contract is a named parse defect not a crash, and every non-authority-contract tree's gate verdict stays byte-identical.
tasks.current: The authority contract's structural invariants live only in the template's human-walked checklist; no parse or gate check reads the file, so a contract that names a current tier absent from the ladder, flips the pointer with no history row (including a wiped or empty change history), drops a history row's attribution, or grants a token that is not a defined action class reads as valid prose and can merge unnoticed.
tasks.desired: A sibling parse of record — not an extension of the entry-anchored ledger parse, which the authority contract's shape does not fit — reads the file's two delimited tables and its current-tier pointer against closed, version-pinned vocabularies of tier names, action-class tokens, and the change-history move enum. The evaluation reports one named defect per violation: a current tier not present in the ladder; a bare pointer flip, defined so that an empty or heading-only change history under a non-initial current tier reds as a missing-history flip and only the born contract's single seed move at the initial tier is exempt; any change-history row missing its date, move-from-the-closed-enum, resulting tier, or evidence refs; and any ladder bundle token that is not a defined action-class token — the structural form of "no never-class act can be granted", never a separate blocklist scan. A wrong or absent template version and an undelimitable region are named parse defects, never a crash or a false pass. The arm registers from its own descriptor file with no merge base required, adding no hand-edited line to the umbrella enumeration, dispatch, or help; it mutates nothing, leaves the existing immutability check's governed set unchanged, and leaves every non-authority-contract tree's verdict byte-identical.

tasks.title: The attribution gate: authorship derivation and protected-path refusal
tasks.goal: A required CI check derives whether each of a PR's diffs is Argus-authored from an in-tree commit trailer read with no ambient credential, refuses the PR when an Argus-authored diff touches a protected path using the shared classifier and scope resolver for the boundary, fails closed when authorship is underivable on a protected-path diff, and never refuses a human-authored diff.
tasks.current: No authorship-scoped merge-boundary refusal exists. A drifted or injected Argus whose protected-path write bypassed the write-time layer reaches the mainline unless a human reviewer notices, and there is no check that fails a PR because an Argus-authored diff touched the authority contract, a governance document, or an out-of-scope file — the sole merge-boundary backstop for the governance-document and out-of-scope classes is a person's attention.
tasks.desired: The gate reads each PR commit's authorship trailer from in-tree commit metadata — never a mutable platform badge, never an ambient credential — and classifies each diff as Argus-authored or not by the trailer's presence. For an Argus-authored diff it applies the shared classifier and scope resolver to the target: a hit on the authority contract, a governance document, or an out-of-declared-scope file refuses the PR with a reason naming the path and the boundary; the out-of-scope boundary's width comes from the resolver's author-independent source, so a self-named broader problem slug cannot reclassify an out-of-scope write as in-scope. When authorship cannot be determined for a diff touching a protected path, that protected-path subset is refused — fail closed — while a non-protected-path diff with an underivable author and any human-authored diff, including a human PR to a protected path, are never refused by this layer. The verdict is structural — trailer presence plus classification — so a planted directive in a commit body or a diff cannot steer it. It composes without editing any shared enumeration line.

tasks.title: The write hook: canonical deny decision and per-CLI fail-closed adapters
tasks.goal: A write-time layer denies a protected-path or out-of-scope write before any bytes through each supported agent CLI's own pre-write hook — one canonical deny decision authored once and reused by per-CLI adapters, each fail-closed — returning a reason naming the path, the boundary, and a remedy, and denying too when scope is unresolvable or the hook process errors.
tasks.current: The agent surface exposes no write-time deny mechanism; the filesystem accepts any write a drive attempts, and the only barrier to a protected-path write is the drive guide's prose plus downstream attention. No pre-write hook is wired to any CLI, and there is no canonical deny decision for a CLI to call.
tasks.desired: One canonical deny decision takes the pending write's target and the drive's declared scope, applies the shared classifier and scope resolver, and returns allow for an in-scope target or deny for a protected-path or out-of-scope target — before any bytes are written — with a reason naming the target path, the boundary it hit, and a remedy. Each supported CLI is wired to that decision through its own pre-write hook as a per-CLI adapter on the vendor-neutral surface, set fail-closed; the deny logic and the protected-path knowledge live once and each CLI's wiring is a pointer, not a content copy, so a portability check finds no divergence and onboarding a CLI is a new adapter file. An unresolvable declared scope denies, and a hook process error, crash, or timeout denies, each with the same three-part reason. A CLI whose hook cannot express a fail-closed deny is listed with the merge-boundary layers as its stated guarantee, never a silent fail-open. The layer is scoped as the write-time layer and makes no claim to stop an out-of-band write.
scope: the canonical deny decision returning allow or a three-part-reason deny, authored once, reusing the shared predicate

tasks.title: The abuse corpus, the honest-layer-split proof, and the bootstrap exception
tasks.goal: The seeded abuse corpus proves each boundary violation is refused by the layer that owns it — the wiped-history self-elevated pointer at the structure arm, the malicious same-PR self-attribution and the widen-slug at the attribution gate, and the out-of-band bypass caught at the merge boundary — while every legitimate case passes with zero false refusals and the non-authority verdict stays byte-identical; and the bootstrap exception and the glossary landings are in place.
tasks.current: The three layers exist and pass their own per-layer fixtures, but nothing proves the cross-layer properties: that each abuse class is red at exactly its owning layer, that the layers compose as honest defense-in-depth, that the legitimate corpus is never falsely refused, and that the merge-boundary layers back up an out-of-band write. No glossary terms are landed and no PR states the introducing-PR bootstrap exception.
tasks.desired: The corpus assembles the abuse fixtures and asserts each is refused at exactly the layer that owns it: the wiped- or empty-history self-elevated authority-contract pointer reds at the structure arm; the first-PR malicious same-PR self-attribution of an out-of-scope code target and the widen-your-own-scope broader-slug case each red at the attribution gate, and the legitimate first-PR case confined to the slug's own document subtrees and the named allowlist passes; the injection-induced protected-path write is denied at the write-time layer and unsteered; and the out-of-band write that bypassed the write-time layer is still refused at the merge boundary — the honest split made concrete. A whole-corpus check shows every legitimate case passes with zero false refusals and the gate's verdict on every non-authority-contract tree is byte-identical with and without the new checks. The candidate glossary terms are landed, and the introducing PR states the incident-bootstrap exception — the merge-boundary check cannot gate the very PR that introduces it, so operator review is that one PR's backstop, and each check gates every subsequent PR.
